_comment: WIMP-nucleon SI rate generation, DAMIC-M halo parameters. Sourced ONLY from pydme (collab_frameworks/pydme/pydme/detector/pattern_efficiency.py has DIFF_A/DIFF_b/sigma_res; collab_frameworks/pydme/pydme/dme_nLL_exclusion.py lines 306-343 has v0/vE/vesc) and this repo own existing defaults (python/ccdarkphys/wimp_nucleon/halo.py, Baxter et al. 2021 convention). v0=238, vesc=544, rho=0.3 agree between pydme and CCDarkSens exactly; vE differs slightly (pydme: 263, CCDarkSens/Baxter: 253.7) -- CCDarkSens own existing default (253.7) used here for internal consistency with the rest of this repo, not pydme own 263. quenching.model=chavarria_izraelevitch_table is this project own best-available quenching model (Chavarria 2016 + Izraelevitch 2017 combined, see quenching.py), NOT a DAMIC-M-specific measurement -- DAMIC-M own quenching calibration, if different, is not available here. UPDATED: sigma grid extended to 1e-45 (was 1e-42), 50 points (was 20) -- the original 1e-42 lower bound was appropriate for DAMIC 2016 but left DAMIC-Ms much better projected sensitivity crossing the exclusion threshold within the first 1-2 grid points, an unresolved grid-edge artifact (q jumped from 0 to >25 between the first two points at every mass tested) rather than real physics.

quenching._comment: chavarria_table = measured Si nuclear recoil ionization efficiency, Chavarria et al. 2016 (Phys. Rev. D 94, 082007), Table I, with linear-to-zero below 0.68 keV_nr (crossing at 0.3 keV_nr per PhysRevD.94.082006) and Lindhard fallback above 2.28 keV_nr (no measurement there). See python/ccdarkphys/wimp_nucleon/quenching.py. Alternative: 'lindhard'.
